title: Govern disaster recovery activation and coordination: decision comparison 1
teachingQuestion: Who declares, restores, validates, accepts, and transitions DR service?
caption: Compare meaning, decision conditions, and failures. These concise distinctions are paired with the worked examples in the teaching unit.

nodes.label: Disaster Recovery Process
nodes.definition: The governed sequence that converts an approved recovery strategy into declaration, notification, assessment, restoration, validation, business acceptance, and return-to-normal activities.
nodes.decision: Approve the process when it assigns accountable roles, activation criteria, communications, dependencies, recovery objectives, and exercise evidence.
nodes.failureExample: An unowned or untested process produces delayed escalation, conflicting actions, or restoration that cannot be accepted safely.
nodes.detail: The governed sequence that converts an approved recovery strategy into declaration, notification, assessment, restoration, validation, business acceptance, and return-to-normal activities.

nodes.label: DR Declaration
nodes.definition: An authorized decision that a disruptive event meets predefined criteria for activating DR governance and recovery resources.
nodes.decision: Declare when verified impact, scope, recovery-objective risk, and designated authority meet the plan’s activation threshold.
nodes.failureExample: Ambiguous authority or thresholds delay escalation or trigger costly recovery without sufficient evidence.
nodes.detail: An authorized decision that a disruptive event meets predefined criteria for activating DR governance and recovery resources.

nodes.label: DR Roles
nodes.definition: Named primary and alternate responsibilities for technical recovery, business decisions, facilities, security, communications, suppliers, and safety.
nodes.decision: Assign roles before disruption; validate contactability, authority, dependencies, and handoffs in exercises.
nodes.failureExample: A generic team list leaves essential decisions or handoffs unowned when a primary person or network is unavailable.
nodes.detail: Named primary and alternate responsibilities for technical recovery, business decisions, facilities, security, communications, suppliers, and safety.

nodes.label: Recovery Team
nodes.definition: The coordinated people who execute technical and business recovery tasks under the assigned recovery authority.
nodes.decision: Staff the team for the affected services, skills, alternates, supplier dependencies, and safe working conditions.
nodes.failureExample: Insufficient skills, absent alternates, or uncoordinated teams can restore components while leaving the service unusable.
nodes.detail: The coordinated people who execute technical and business recovery tasks under the assigned recovery authority.

nodes.label: Crisis Communications
nodes.definition: Controlled, audience-specific communications that keep staff, leaders, customers, suppliers, and authorities informed using resilient channels.
nodes.decision: Use approved messages, owners, cadence, escalation paths, and alternate channels appropriate to the event and audience.
nodes.failureExample: Unverified or inconsistent messages create unsafe actions, regulatory exposure, or loss of stakeholder trust.
nodes.detail: Controlled, audience-specific communications that keep staff, leaders, customers, suppliers, and authorities informed using resilient channels.

nodes.label: Damage Assessment
nodes.definition: A rapid, evidence-based determination of affected people, facilities, systems, data, identities, dependencies, and recovery-option viability.
nodes.decision: Assess before selecting restoration actions; preserve evidence and update scope as facts change.
nodes.failureExample: Restoring on unverified assumptions can spread compromise, overlook dependencies, or choose an unavailable alternate strategy.
nodes.detail: A rapid, evidence-based determination of affected people, facilities, systems, data, identities, dependencies, and recovery-option viability.

nodes.label: DR Training
nodes.definition: Role-specific preparation that enables people to execute recovery procedures, communications, safety actions, and decision handoffs.
nodes.decision: Train before an event and refresh after role, system, supplier, or plan changes; verify with exercises.
nodes.failureExample: Reading a plan does not demonstrate that personnel can coordinate safely under time pressure.
nodes.detail: Role-specific preparation that enables people to execute recovery procedures, communications, safety actions, and decision handoffs.

nodes.label: DR Lessons Learned
nodes.definition: Evidence-supported findings from events or exercises that lead to owned corrective actions, plan updates, and retests.
nodes.decision: Record observed versus expected results, assign owner/due date/evidence, then retest material changes.
nodes.failureExample: Closing an exercise with an attendance record or unowned notes repeats the same readiness gap.
nodes.detail: Evidence-supported findings from events or exercises that lead to owned corrective actions, plan updates, and retests.

nodes.label: Recovery Authority
nodes.definition: The delegated decision right to activate DR, commit resources, accept service restoration, manage exceptions, and end recovery status.
nodes.decision: Document authority limits, alternates, business acceptance roles, and escalation paths before disruption.
nodes.failureExample: A technical team must not silently substitute for business acceptance or commit resources outside its authority.
nodes.detail: The delegated decision right to activate DR, commit resources, accept service restoration, manage exceptions, and end recovery status.
